label: prop:content-genfun-palindromic
title: The content generating function $C_n(q) = \sum_\lambda f^\lambda q^{\mathrm{content}(\lambda)}$ is palindromic and bar-even
html:
Proposition (palindromy and bar-even rigidity of the content generating function).

For n \geq 1 let f^\lambda be the number of standard Young tableaux of shape \lambda \vdash n and \mathrm{content}(\lambda) = \sum_{(i,j)\in\lambda}(j-i) the content sum, and set

C_n(q) \;=\; \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} f^\lambda\, q^{\,\mathrm{content}(\lambda)} .

Then C_n is palindromic,

C_n(q) \;=\; C_n(q^{-1}),

and its deviation from the classical value is bar-even of second order,

C_n(q) - C_n(1) \;=\; O\!\big((q-1)^2\big),
\qquad C_n(1) = \sum_{\lambda\vdash n} f^\lambda = I(n),

where I(n) is the number of involutions of S_n.

By prop:binding-period-involution-statistic, C_n(q) is the content-only face of the binding statistic — the object obtained by retaining the RSK shape and discarding the descent (major-index) data. The bar-even O((q-1)^2) deviation is exactly the q-rigidity measured for the level-1/2 alien datum \Delta_{\omega_0}: the content sector carries no linear q-deformation, so it activates only at second order.

Both statements are instances of a single structural fact — partition conjugation \lambda \mapsto \lambda' is an anti-invariant involution, f^{\lambda'} = f^\lambda and \mathrm{content}(\lambda') = -\mathrm{content}(\lambda) — which is proved for every n in the library module QOU.AntiInvolutionPalindrome (palindromic_sum_of_antiInvolution for the palindromy, and first_moment_zero_of_antiInvolution, \sum_\lambda f^\lambda\,\mathrm{content}(\lambda) = 0, for the vanishing linear term). The Lean sibling here records the fully machine-checked n=4 instance, C_4(q) = q^6 + 3q^2 + 2 + 3q^{-2} + q^{-6}.
